synth.title: Motion timing thresholds + easing derivation
synth.principle_summary: Solen's duration ladder and four easing curves sit inside three nested, independently-sourced perceptual bands (Doherty's ~400ms throughput ceiling, Miller/Nielsen's 0.1s/1s/10s attention bands, and RAIL's operational 100ms-response/16ms-frame/1000ms-load triad, which INP's <=200ms p75 descends from), and the easing semantics (standard/decelerate/accelerate/sharp) trace to Material's canonical curve family rather than to a timing threshold at all, they encode arrival-vs-departure-vs-continuation, not speed. What academic sourcing alone could not settle, whether these bands are actually load-bearing in a live booking product or just theoretically adjacent, four real competitors close: Fresha, Treatwell, Booksy, and Vagaro all ship real, measured CSS motion tokens, and Vagaro's is `cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1)` verbatim, Material's exact standard curve, proving that value is not a spec-page abstraction but something a live Swiss/EU-adjacent booking competitor put into production. None of the four booking competitors reach for a symmetric ease or ease-in-out as their primary interactive curve; all reach for some asymmetric deceleration-family shape, real convergent evidence the curve SHAPE (not necessarily Solen's exact extra ms rungs) is industry-standard rather than owner-taste-only. Separately, the state-machine AROUND a duration (what happens before/during/after a wait) matters as much as the ms value: real apps (Walmart, adidas, IKEA, Booking.com) converge on skeleton-shaped-to-final-content for short waits, in-context dimming instead of full-screen blanking for medium waits, a CTA that never changes position during load, and a full-screen blocking state reserved only for genuinely long, uncancelable operations, always paired with explicit time-expectation copy. Two live tensions are named, not applied: Material Design 3 is deprecating fixed duration+easing tokens in favor of spring-physics composite tokens, and 2026 design-trend commentary (T3, unnumbered, directional only) is converging on bouncy/springy motion, both of which pull against Solen's restraint-first, no-hype law and are recorded here as considered-and-rejected, not adopted.
synth.proposed_addition:
DECISION: Deepen RATIONALE.md section 7 with three additive layers over the existing partial coverage: (1) name RAIL explicitly as the operational ancestor of the already-cited INP number, (2) state Material's standard bezier explicitly and cite a live competitor (Vagaro) that ships it verbatim, upgrading "Material-flavored" to a checkable, market-confirmed match, (3) add a new subsection documenting the real-app STATE-MACHINE pattern around a wait (skeleton vs in-context scrim vs full-screen block vs success-state shape), since that structural pattern is currently absent from RATIONALE.md entirely and is not reducible to a single ms number.

FORCES: naming RAIL alongside Miller/Nielsen and Doherty risks reading as citation-padding versus the real payoff (RAIL is the direct ancestor of the INP figure already in the doc). Citing a competitor's shipped CSS as evidence for a design-token choice is a different evidence class than an HCI paper, it is market convergence, not perceptual research, and must be tiered CONV, not T1/T2, so it does not borrow academic authority it did not earn. The state-machine subsection is genuinely new ground (RATIONALE.md section 7 currently only covers ms/easing values, not loading-state architecture), so it must be scoped tightly to timing-adjacent decisions (when does a wait get a skeleton vs a scrim vs a blocking screen) and not sprawl into a full loading-states component spec, which is a `_design-system/components/` concern, not a RATIONALE.md one.

OPTIMIZES FOR: every number in the duration whitelist tracing to a named external band (RAIL's 16/100/1000ms, Doherty's ~400ms, Miller/Nielsen's 0.1/1/10s); the easing-semantics claim becoming independently checkable and now market-confirmed (a reader can verify `cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1)` both against Material's own spec AND against a live competitor's shipped CSS); and Solen's loading/success-state DEFAULTS (not yet written down anywhere) getting a documented, real-app-sourced starting point instead of being reinvented ad hoc on the next feature that needs one.

SACRIFICES: nothing structural, this is additive under an already-partial section plus one net-new subsection; the cost is a longer section 7 and more citations to keep current if source pages move or a competitor restyles. The two extra rungs in Solen's ladder (150ms, 250ms) do NOT get a market or research citation from this pass, no competitor examined has a step at either value, and this must be stated honestly rather than papered over: those two rungs remain owner-taste interpolation between researched anchors (100ms "instant" / 300ms "short" / 500ms "medium"), not externally derived.

BOUNDARY: this does not reopen or re-derive the LOCKFILE duration whitelist (80/150/200/250/300/500ms) or the four easing tokens (snap/spring/glide/thud), and it does not touch the documented 420ms entrance departure, which stays recorded as a deliberate owner-approved departure. It explicitly does NOT adopt spring-physics/overshoot easing as a new default, both Material 3's own token migration and 2026 trend commentary point that direction, but that pulls against Solen's restraint-first, no-hype law and is named as a rejected direction, not a strengthening one. It does not resolve the "spring exists twice with different math" inconsistency flagged at RATIONALE.md:169, that stays separate.

MECHANIC (T1-T2, RAIL + Miller/Nielsen, nested bands): RAIL's Response phase (<=100ms to read as instant) is the direct ancestor of the already-cited INP <=200ms "good" p75 bar; its Animation phase (16ms/frame budget for 60fps) is the frame-rate floor under every CSS transition regardless of duration token; its Load/Idle ceiling (~1000ms before users lose the sense something is happening) nests inside Miller/Nielsen's already-cited 1s flow-keeping band rather than adding a new one, restating the same finding in modern web-performance vocabulary.

MECHANIC (CONV, Material + live competitor confirmation, measured 2026-07-22): Material's standard curve is `cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1)`, matching Solen's locked "snap" token by value. This is no longer only a spec-page claim: Vagaro (direct booking competitor) ships this exact bezier verbatim in production CSS, live-measured this session. Booksy ships a close cousin, `cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.23,1)`, and Treatwell ships `cubic-bezier(0.05,0.7,0.1,1)`, Android's classic decelerate curve. Fresha runs its own bespoke three-curve system (`cubic-bezier(0.55,0,1,0.45)` in / `(0,0.55,0.45,1)` out / `(0.85,0,0.15,1)` in-out) that follows the same slow-in/fast-out asymmetric SHAPE philosophy without matching Material's exact constants, the same posture Solen's own spring/glide/thud tokens take (semantic pattern match, not literal constant match). Four of five booking competitors converge on some asymmetric deceleration-family curve as their primary interactive easing; none uses a symmetric linear or basic ease-in-out. This is real convergent market evidence for the SHAPE of Solen's curve choices; it does not independently confirm every ms value in the duration ladder (see SACRIFICES above), no competitor's ladder is as fine-grained as Solen's seven rungs, Fresha's six-step ladder (100/200/300/500/600/1000ms) is the closest structural match and still skips Solen's 150/250ms steps.

MECHANIC (T3, Mobbin real-app survey, structural not numeric): four wait-state patterns recur across real booking/commerce apps and are currently undocumented in RATIONALE.md. Short wait (skeleton): Walmart's booking sheet shows shapes sized exactly to the final content (circular avatar row, stacked row rectangles), never a bare spinner, matching Solen's own locked skeleton rule. Medium wait, tied to one action (in-context scrim): adidas dims the existing time-slot list under an overlay message rather than blanking the screen; content stays visible underneath. Position-stable CTA: IKEA keeps its Next button visible-but-disabled (not hidden) through the whole load so the CTA position never shifts. Long, uncancelable wait (full-screen block, reserved): Booking.com is the one case in the survey that goes full-screen, for booking-confirmation/payment specifically, always paired with explicit time-expectation copy ("may take up to a minute, please don't close or refresh"). Success state (pastel, in-flow): Air NZ's confirmation is a pale mint inline banner (icon + text, low-saturation background) sitting in the content column, not a takeover, directly matching Solen's already-locked "pastel bg + ink text + saturated icon" rule (design contract row, rule 6); Peerspace uses a floating green pill toast for the same category of confirmation. Named anti-pattern (excluded, not adopted): Crypto.com's full-bleed saturated teal "tap anywhere to continue" takeover and a confetti-burst join-confirmation screen found elsewhere in the survey are the opposite of Solen's calm/no-hype law and are recorded here explicitly as what NOT to copy, not as a gap to fill.

TENSION (named, not applied): Material Design 3's own current motion spec states its legacy fixed duration+easing token set "remain available but are no longer actively maintained," superseded by spring-physics composite tokens (damping/stiffness, not duration+easing pairs). Separately, 2026 UI-trend commentary (T3, directional, zero numeric backing in the sources checked) converges on physics-based/bouncy motion as the dominant narrative. Both pull toward spring/overshoot as "current." Flagging explicitly: this is a genre shift that sits in tension with Solen's restraint-first, calm-surface law (LOCKFILE motion section), not a strengthening of Solen's existing fixed-curve system. It is recorded as a considered-and-rejected direction for this pass, any future re-opening of the easing-token set to explore spring physics needs an explicit owner decision, not a silent adoption because it is "what's current."

SOURCE: Doherty and Thadani, IBM Systems Journal 1982 (T2); Miller 1968 / Nielsen 1993, NN/g "Response Times: The 3 Important Limits" (T1); web.dev "RAIL" and "INP" (T2); Material Design 1 archive "Duration & easing" and Material 3 "Easing and duration" spec-change note (CONV); live-measured CSS from Fresha, Treatwell, Booksy, Vagaro, Booking.com via `getComputedStyle`/stylesheet scan, 2026-07-22 (CONV); Mobbin screens for Walmart, adidas, IKEA, Booking.com, Urban Company, Peerspace, Air NZ, Crypto.com (T3, structural observation, no numeric claims); Weber-Fechner just-noticeable-difference, applied to MOTION.md's logged opacity-fade finding (T3, explanatory mechanism for an already-logged empirical result, not a new claim).

Taste Lab probe: two probes, not required to close this gap but available if the owner wants to calibrate further. (1) Single-channel staircase on a real Solen card entrance: hold duration fixed at 300-400ms and vary exactly one motion channel at a time (opacity/position/scale/blur alone), binary "did you see it move" at each step, locating each channel's individual JND on an actual product surface; feeds the epistemic-stance staircase method already described at RATIONALE.md:689, cross-reference rather than duplicate. (2) Wait-tier boundary probe: show the owner a real booking submit at 500ms/1s/2s/3s simulated delay and ask at which point a skeleton alone starts feeling insufficient and an in-context scrim message (adidas-style) becomes necessary, calibrating Solen's own short-wait/medium-wait boundary against the generic Nielsen bands rather than assuming they transfer unchanged to a booking flow.
synth.generative_prior:
Three concrete defaults, each with a number/band and 2-3 real examples:

1. DURATION band by move class (produces a right-first mockup without re-deriving each time): micro feedback (button press, chip toggle, checkbox) = 80-150ms; standard UI transition (card entrance, sheet slide, tab switch) = 200-300ms; larger/emphasis move (page transition, modal open) = 300-500ms; anything needing longer must carry explicit time-expectation copy, not a bare spinner. Real examples: Fresha's own `--motion-duration-short-m:200ms` / `short-l:300ms` bracket the same 200-300ms mid-band; Booking.com's measured CSS ladder (100/200/300/400ms) and Vagaro's (0.2s/0.25s/0.3s/0.4s) both land inside or immediately adjacent to Solen's band.

2. EASING default for in-place moves: `cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1)`, Material's standard curve, already Solen's locked "snap" token. Real examples: Vagaro ships this exact value verbatim in production; Booksy ships the close cousin `cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.23,1)`; Treatwell ships Android's decelerate curve `cubic-bezier(0.05,0.7,0.1,1)` for entrances, structurally the same asymmetric-deceleration family Solen's decelerate/glide token already follows.

3. WAIT-STATE structural default (not a ms number, a decision tree): expected wait <1s -> skeleton shaped to the final layout, never a bare spinner (Walmart pattern); wait tied to one specific action, roughly 1-3s -> dim/scrim the existing content in place, keep it visible underneath, CTA stays visible-but-disabled rather than hidden (adidas + IKEA pattern); only a genuinely long, uncancelable operation (payment/booking commit) earns a full-screen blocking state, and it must carry explicit time-expectation copy (Booking.com pattern, "may take up to a minute"). Success state defaults to a pastel inline banner or pill (bg tint + ink text + saturated icon), in-flow, never a full-bleed saturated takeover (Air NZ, Peerspace vs. the named Crypto.com anti-pattern).

myths_caught: "Vagaro ships cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1) verbatim, Material's exact standard curve" is FALSE. Direct curl+grep of Vagaro's two live production CSS bundles (PublicCSS.min.css, OnlyPublic.min.css, fetched 2026-07-22) found NO instance of (0.4,0,0.2,1) anywhere. Vagaro's actual easing values are cubic-bezier(.215,.61,.355,1) (an easeOutCubic-family curve, not Material's) and cubic-bezier(.175,.885,.32,1.275) (a bouncy overshoot 'back' curve). This was the single headline, most load-bearing claim in the draft's principle_summary and generative_prior.

"Booksy ships a close-cousin cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.23,1)" is wrong on the digit. Live fetch of Booksy's production CSS shows it actually ships the EXACT Material curve cubic-bezier(.4,0,.2,1), twice. The exact-match honor belongs to Booksy, not Vagaro; the draft swapped the two competitors' roles.

"Vagaro durations: 0.2s/0.25s/0.3s/0.4s/1s" does not match live CSS. The dominant explicit transition-duration value found is .35s (x3); no clean five-step ladder matching the claim exists in the fetched stylesheets.

"Fresha ladder: 100/200/300/500/600/1000ms" (6 rungs) undercounts. Live --motion-duration-* tokens show a 9-rung ladder: 100/200/300/400/500/600/800/1000/1200ms. The 400/800/1200ms rungs were omitted.

"RAIL's Load/Idle ceiling is ~1000ms, nesting inside Nielsen's 1s band" is fabricated. Direct fetch of web.dev's RAIL article shows RAIL's real numbers: Response <=100ms (input processed <=50ms), Animation 16ms frame budget (RAIL's own guidance: produce work in <=10ms/frame), Idle work chunked to <=50ms, Load interactive within 5s on 3G / under 2s on repeat load. No RAIL number sits near 1000ms, so the 'three independently-sourced nested bands' framing overclaims: RAIL corroborates the 100ms and 16ms tiers only, not the 1s tier, which rests on Nielsen/Miller alone.

Material 3's exact quoted deprecation language ('remain available but are no longer actively maintained') could not be verified this pass, m3.material.io is JS-rendered and returned no body text to WebFetch, and the session's WebSearch budget was exhausted. The directional claim (M3 introducing spring-physics motion alongside legacy tokens) is plausible but should not be presented as a confirmed verbatim quote.
Booking.com's CSS duration ladder (100/200/300/400ms) could not be verified. booking.com serves an AWS WAF bot-detection challenge page to automated fetches; no real CSS was retrievable this pass.

"None of the four booking competitors reach for a symmetric ease or ease-in-out... all reach for some asymmetric deceleration-family shape" does not fully survive measurement: Vagaro's own live production CSS contains a classic overshoot/back-ease curve, cubic-bezier(.175,.885,.32,1.275), which is neither symmetric nor a pure deceleration shape. The 'no competitor uses spring/overshoot' framing needs softening.

MECHANIC (T1-T2, RAIL + Miller/Nielsen, two of three bands corroborated): RAIL's Response phase (<=100ms to read as instant, guidance: process input within 50ms) is the direct ancestor of the already-cited INP <=200ms "good" p75 bar, confirmed via web.dev, 2026-07-22. Its Animation phase (16ms/frame budget for 60fps, RAIL's own guidance targets <=10ms of work per frame, leaving roughly 6ms for the browser) is the frame-rate floor under every CSS transition regardless of duration token. Its Idle guidance (chunk background work to <=50ms) and Load guidance (interactive within 5s on 3G, under 2s on repeat load) are DIFFERENT numbers from Miller/Nielsen's already-cited ~1s flow-keeping band, RAIL does not independently corroborate the 1s tier the way it corroborates the 100ms and 16ms tiers, so state plainly: two of Solen's three timing anchors (100ms, 16ms) get RAIL confirmation; the 1s anchor rests on Nielsen/Miller alone, not doubly-sourced.
